newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ ELECTION - Party policies on foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: NZ ELECTION - Party policies on foreign investment.

text.p: The following is an outline of the stance of New Zealand's main political parties on the issues of foreign ownership in New Zealand, land sales and tariffs on imports.
A general election is due on Saturday.
NEW ZEALAND FIRST
* Would limit foreign investment and ownership in strategic assets, including utilities, to 24.9 percent.
* Not opposed to foreign investment, but must be to New Zealand's advantage.
* Supports tariff reduction programme but would review the timetable
* Reserves the right to impose retaliatory tariffs on countries which have trade barriers against NZ products.
NATIONAL
* Strongly in favour of foreign investment in New Zealand, believing it is crucial to the well-being of the country's economy.
* Favours a further lowering of tariffs across the board, and a full review in 1998.
* Tariffs to maximum of five percent by year 2000, with exceptions for cars, textiles, and footwear.
ALLIANCE
* Would halt rural land sales to foreigners.
* Other land sales to foreigners would face national interest test.
* Ministerial approval needed for foreign purchases of more than 25 percent of a company's shares.
* Raise tariffs to 10 percent on imports except from Australia.
LABOUR
* Sees rural and pastoral land sales to foreigners as "a special case". Otherwise welcomes foreign investment
* Supports phased tariff reductions but with a slower timetable than National for textiles, cars and footwear.
* Promote freer trade through the WTO.
ACT
* For complete tariff elimination.
* For privatisation and against any constraints on foreign investment. Wants to encourage New Zealanders to save more.
CHRISTIAN COALITION
* Mirrors National in approach to tariffs.
* Would tighten rules on foreign ownership of rural land.
UNITED
* Mirrors National's approach to tariffs and foreign investment.
-- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
